themes.consensus_view: Banks broadly agree that AI infrastructure spending is the dominant earnings driver across hardware, semis, and power, though a minority warn the rally is now leaning on positioning (levered ETFs) and unit economics that may not justify the spend.

facts_agreed.claim: AI infrastructure spending is driving an outsized share of S&P 500 earnings growth and hardware revenue beats.
evidence_quotes: The beneficiaries of AI infrastructure investment will account for roughly half of S&P 500 EPS growth
DELL should trade higher on an earnings beat & better-than-expected FY27 guidance
The ramp in AI demand thus far in '26 has been astonishing.
surging demand outpacing the capacity being built resulting in sustainably strong demand
Semiconductors, Techm Hardware and Industrials... swept up by a more powerful structural influence of Hyperscaler capex.

facts_agreed.claim: Demand for AI compute is outrunning supply, shifting pricing power to hardware and memory suppliers.
evidence_quotes: pricing power has shifted decisively back to suppliers
surging demand outpacing the capacity being built resulting in sustainably strong demand
ASML's visibility into 2027 and 2028 only suggests that the semiconductor capex cycle has more upside.
Dell is being re-priced for extreme monetisation of AI compute infrastructure demand

facts_agreed.claim: The AI infrastructure trade is the largest and most-traded theme in the market, with investors positioned accordingly.
evidence_quotes: the market has been rational in trading the largest current theme
investors continue to climb a Tech cycle wall of worry

facts_contested.claim: Whether the AI rally is supported by genuine fundamentals or increasingly by market-structure flows and questionable unit economics.
facts_contested.for_evidence: The ramp in AI demand thus far in '26 has been astonishing.
facts_contested.against_evidence: the AI trade is no longer just being driven by fundamentals

facts_contested.claim: Whether current enterprise AI spending is producing useful output to justify the capex.
facts_contested.for_evidence: surging demand outpacing the capacity being built resulting in sustainably strong demand
facts_contested.against_evidence: token consumption is increasingly difficult to tie to useful output

themes.consensus_view: Banks broadly flag the Strait of Hormuz closure as a live oil supply and inflation risk, but split on whether a US-Iran deal is imminent or the closure drags into September.

facts_agreed.claim: The Strait of Hormuz status is a key live catalyst for oil supply, inflation, and broader risk markets, widely referenced across desks.

facts_contested.claim: Timing of a US-Iran deal and Strait reopening
facts_contested.for_evidence: We are more constructive than consensus on the prospects for a US-Iran deal
facts_contested.against_evidence: Strait is likely to remain mostly closed through to September

themes.consensus_view: Banks broadly treat a US-Iran ceasefire as a live near-term catalyst that has already driven oil lower and equities higher, but most desks have not staked a directional call beyond flagging it as a rotation risk.

facts_agreed.claim: Mounting hopes for a US-Iran peace deal have been a key driver of the recent risk-on tone, pushing oil down and equities up.
evidence_quotes: a real US-Iran deal would likely turn that risk-on tone into a rotation
markets put in a strong performance overall, driven by mounting hopes for some kind of peace deal

facts_agreed.claim: Major desks are tracking the US-Iran ceasefire as an active negotiation and a primary macro catalyst this window.

themes.consensus_view: Tech and software stocks have ripped higher with major inflows and a multi-week winning streak, but banks are split on whether the rally can continue given extreme crowding and stretched positioning.

facts_agreed.claim: Software has staged a powerful multi-week rally with strong institutional participation.
evidence_quotes: Software ETF on pace for 7th straight weekly gain up 36% over that span.
Software was up 20%+ in May, its best month since 2002

facts_agreed.claim: Tech positioning and crowding have reached extreme levels across institutional metrics.
evidence_quotes: The move is now visible across virtually every institutional positioning metric.
Key near-term risk is a reversal in Tech/AI momentum and beta crowding

facts_contested.claim: Whether the tech/equity rally can continue from here
facts_contested.for_evidence: Software ETF on pace for 7th straight weekly gain up 36% over that span.
facts_contested.against_evidence: the tactical setup is getting full and the yards will likely be harder

themes.consensus_view: Banks broadly flag the rapid doubling of levered single-stock ETF assets as a live positioning risk, with Goldman and Nomura quantifying the buildup and The Market Ear warning the unwind could be disorderly.

facts_agreed.claim: Multiple banks flag levered single-stock ETFs and the leverage they introduce as a key market structure dynamic to watch.
evidence_quotes: Systemic leverage in index swaps and ETFs
there are a number of catalysts for this to suffer a "messy" unwind

themes.consensus_view: Banks agree the rally is broadening beyond mega-cap tech, with equal-weight indices, small-caps, and wider earnings revisions joining the move.

facts_agreed.claim: The rally is widening beyond mega-cap tech as equal-weight indices and broader earnings sentiment improve.
evidence_quotes: The equal-weight S&P 500 and the Dow made new highs Tuesday.
earnings sentiment (the rate of upward EPS estimate revisions) is now improving broadly
